name: Rolling Kitchen Cart
pitch: A rolling cart for toasters and panini presses: 13 slot rows for shelves on a 50 mm pitch, an optional drawer, locking casters, and one dense 4x8 sheet.

parameters.name: width
parameters.limits: 450-750 mm (over 750 would need a centre post; not modeled)

stages.title: Cut the sheet
stages.detail: Cut the fit-test coupon first (slot = tab + 0.1 mm), then the 29-part sheet from the DXF (CUT layer): 50 m of path. The cart is the densest nest: expect a long run, so check the sheet is flat and weighted before starting.

stages.title: Remove char and sand
stages.detail: Brush the char off every edge, sand 120 then 180 grit, ease the worktop edge and the shelf fronts by hand.

stages.title: Dry fit
stages.detail: Stand SIDE-L and SIDE-R on BASE, add BACK, RAILs, the worktop, and slide in a SHELF on its LEDGERs. Check the shelf-slot pitch (50 mm) and that the tabs end flush.

stages.title: Pre-finish
stages.detail: Seal every face now, the worktop most of all (kitchen use: water-based poly, 3 coats on top). Mask the tabs and slots so the glue bonds to bare wood.

stages.title: Feet and casters
stages.detail: Glue and screw the FOOT-A and FOOT-B pairs under the base (8 x #8 x 1-3/4 in), then bolt the 4 casters on the 73.2 x 44.5 mm pattern with M8 bolts and nuts. Fit at least 2 locking casters.

stages.title: Glue-up (Titebond III)
stages.detail: Glue SIDE-L and SIDE-R onto BASE, the BACK, then the three RAILs, then set the worktop over the side tabs. Clamp across the width and check diagonals.

stages.title: Screws as clamps
stages.detail: 45 #8 screws in all: #8 x 1-1/2 in through the side faces and top; #8 x 1-1/4 in for rails and shelf locks. Pilots are laser-cut at 3.0 mm.

stages.title: Shelves and ledgers
stages.detail: Screw a LEDGER pair into the slot row you choose, then drop in the SHELF and lock it with the 2 SHELF-LOCK screws. Move rows in 50 mm steps for tall appliances.

stages.title: Optional drawer and cleat
stages.detail: Drawer: glue the finger-jointed box, drop in the bottom, screw DRW-FACE, set on its DRAW ledgers. Cleat: glue the two CLEAT-BACKER layers to the back and fit the Z-bar. A loaded cart is not wall-hung: use the cleat for an empty/tidy-storage version only.

stages.title: Finish, load test, pack
stages.detail: Final coat, 24 h cure, a 40 kg load test rolled across a doorstep, lock check on a slope, then flat-pack.

materials.sheet: 18 mm (3/4 in) sanded plywood (basic birch-faced or cabinet ply), 4 x 8 ft x 1

hardware.item: 3 in locking swivel casters (73.2 x 44.5 mm plate, M8)

materials.finish: water-based poly, 3 coats on the worktop (about $14)

safety: Locking casters: lock at least two on any loaded or worktop use.
Cart load rating is untested: target 40 kg shelves + 20 kg worktop, UNVERIFIED. Load test every design change.
Tip: the cart is 900 mm tall and narrow; keep heavy appliances on the lowest shelves and do not roll over thresholds loaded.
Do not run heat-producing appliances on the ply unprotected: use a trivet.
Not a children's product (no CPSIA testing).

profit.labels: ESTIMATES AND ASSUMPTIONS ONLY - not quotes, not guaranteed, machine time NOT measured on the real machine
profit.assumptions: All dollar figures are planning ESTIMATES / ASSUMPTIONS, not quotes, not guaranteed. Sheet prices: 4x8 ft 18 mm birch plywood $70-110, basic plywood $55-75 (assumption). Machine time uses a sourced RANGE for a 120 W diode on 18 mm ply (low 120 / typical 300 / high 600 mm/min effective, i.e. after multiple passes; see CUT-SPEED-RESEARCH.md); ACMER publishes no 18 mm ply feed rate, so none of it is measured on this machine. Machine wear/electricity $1.70 per machine-hour (assumption). Labor valued at $25/h for the "after labor" line only. Marketplace fees 10% (assumption, e.g. Etsy-style).

machine_time.label: ESTIMATE. Diode = ACMER X1 Ultra 120 W on 18 mm plywood; effective rate = speed / passes. Includes rapid travel between contours and 15 min per sheet of load/focus/unload. Not measured.

commercial_laser.label: ASSUMPTION. Sourced case: 300-600 W CO2 flatbed, single pass at ~600 mm/min (vendor 480-720), 60 m/min rapids, 5 min/sheet, $8/h operating cost. What-if cases: a machine 10x / 20x faster than the diode mid cut+travel time (not sourced for 18 mm ply).

profit.price_band_source: ASSUMPTION (not in SHORTLIST.md): $180-$420 band, set against 2-shelf rolling kitchen carts at roughly $70-$250 retail [third-party estimate]
profit.note_machine_time: ESTIMATE: 3.2 h (low-speed case 7.5 h, best case 1.7 h) of machine time per unit for 50 m of cut path in 1 sheet(s) on a 120 W diode, 18 mm plywood. Machine time, not material, is still the limit on profit per hour, but a single test cut on scrap will replace this range with a real number.

unverified: Machine time is an estimate (120 W diode on 18 mm ply, sourced range, not measured on this machine); cut time and profit/hour depend on it.
Price band is my assumption (cart is not in SHORTLIST.md).
Caster price and fit are from the original design; the hole pattern is assumed for common 3 in plate casters.
Depth and width ranges were build-checked only at the stress variants (400-520 mm deep, 480-800 mm wide).
